The v2 JSON API requires token authentication for access; authentication is not treated as a grant of proprietary rights. Only public ADS bibliographic metadata is retained. CTAS does not download, mirror, or assert reuse rights for article full text; publisher and repository links retain their own access and reuse terms. Event association requires an exact retained transient name.

No automated provider-data request was sent. The official legacy HTTPS query form requires reCAPTCHA and says users needing more than 100 light curves should contact ASAS-SN. The published V2 client and documentation currently use an unencrypted HTTP API, while the linked HTTPS V2 host and client repository are unavailable. CTAS therefore withholds automatic ingestion until ASAS-SN publishes a current secure, bounded machine-access contract. This is an interface-integrity boundary, not a claim that the public light-curve data are proprietary.
